newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada monthly GDP falls 0.2 percent in December.
newsitem.headline: Canada monthly GDP falls 0.2 percent in December.

text.p: Canada's real gross domestic product, seasonally adjusted, fell 0.2 percent in December after rising 0.4 percent in November, Statistics Canada said on Friday.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast real GDP to rise 0.1 percent in December.
Note: GDP figures are in billions of dollars, seasonally adjusted at annual rates at factor cost, constant 1986 dollars.
Statistics Canada said that despite the December decline, the Canadian economy grew at an average 0.2 percent a month during the fourth quarter of 1996.
The decline in the overall GDP in December was due mainly to lower manufacturing production and output of utilities. Retail trade and transportation services also fell in the month.

The decline was partially offset by gains in the financial and related services sector, as well as community, business and personal services, and wholesale trade. Activity in construction and communications services also rose.
(For more information from Statistics Canada contact Michel Girard, Industry Measures and Analysis Division, at 613-951-9145).
